questions.q: What does reinstating a retired asset do?
options: Creates a brand-new asset with a new date placed in service
Permanently deletes the asset's transaction history
Transfers the asset to a different book
Reverses the retirement, restoring the asset's in-service status and undoing its gain/loss calculation
questions.explain: Reinstatement restores an asset to in-service status, reverses its retirement gain/loss, and resumes depreciation with continuity.

questions.q: How does reinstatement differ from simply adding the asset back as a new addition?
options: There is no difference between the two approaches
Reinstatement preserves the asset's original identity and depreciation history; a new addition starts a fresh schedule
A new addition is always faster to process
Reinstatement can only be used for CIP assets
questions.explain: Reinstatement preserves the original date placed in service and accumulated depreciation history, unlike a fresh addition which starts an entirely new schedule.

options: Because reinstatement can only be done on the same calendar day as the retirement
Because Oracle Fusion Assets charges a fee for late reinstatements
Because reinstatement is only available for tax books
Because once accounting has been created and the period closed, reversing it runs into the one-way calendar problem
questions.explain: Reinstatement is clean before a retirement's accounting is created and the period closes; afterward, the one-way depreciation calendar makes a clean reversal much harder.

questions.q: When is reinstatement the correct transaction to use?
options: When an asset was correctly retired and is being replaced with a new purchase
When a retirement was erroneous or premature and needs to be undone
When an asset simply needs to be transferred to a new location
When an asset's category needs correcting
questions.explain: Reinstatement specifically reverses a mistaken or premature retirement; a genuine replacement purchase is a new addition instead.

questions.q: If an asset is genuinely retired and later replaced with a similar but different physical asset, what is the correct transaction for the replacement?
options: Reinstating the original retired asset
A cost adjustment on the retired asset
A reclassification of the retired asset
A brand-new asset addition
questions.explain: Since the original retirement wasn't an error, the replacement is a distinct new purchase and should be entered as a new addition, not a reinstatement.
